title: Introduce host-side rendezvous shim to coalesce small prefill copies and reduce thread contention
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background:
Host-side overhead for prefill->decode handoff is dominating 95th percentile latency for short requests. Small, highly concurrent prefill copies and many lightweight thread wakeups during bursty traffic create contention in the host threadpool and thrash NUMA-local cache lines. Our existing approach schedules each prefill as a separate copy job and immediately enqueues a decode work item; this creates many tiny GPU memcpy ops and per-request scheduling cost.

Goal:
Reduce CPU-side overhead and amortize memcpy/handshake cost by introducing a light-weight 'rendezvous shim' that batches tiny prefill copies into larger coalesced DMA windows and smooths threadpool wakeups (handoff quanta). The shim should be transparent to callers, work with pinned and pageable allocations, respect NUMA affinity, and integrate with the kernel-selection heuristics so we don't regress long-sequence throughput.

Proposed design:
1) Rendezvous shim component in host pipeline that sits between prefill aggregation and GPU submission. It groups contiguous small staging buffers targeting the same GPU slice and issues a single fused memcpy when possible. Batching keys: destination GPU, sequence id, timestamp window (approx 500us), and preferred memory type (pinned vs pageable).
2) Hand-off quanta and thread parking: instead of immediate per-request decode enqueue, the shim releases a limited number of decode work items per wakeup (configurable quanta). If backlog is small, it releases immediately; if backlog is high, it applies an exponential backoff per source thread to avoid threadpool hammering.
3) NUMA-aware coalescing: use a lightweight NUMA hint layer to avoid cross-node copies for buffers allocated on a specific socket; prefer merging only if source buffers share a NUMA domain.
4) Kernel-selection integration: expose shim metrics (avg coalesced bytes, coalesce rate, average quanta size) to the kernel picker so it can favor kernels that benefit from larger batch sizes, and fallback to low-latency kernels for cases where coalescing is disabled.
5) Fallbacks & safety: if a buffer is registered for async pinned DMA (pinned_by_runtime flag) do direct submit; if coalescing would increase latency beyond request SLO (tracked via per-request deadlines) skip batching for that request.

Acceptance criteria:
- 95th percentile end-to-end prefill-to-first-decode latency reduced by >=30% for bursty short requests (<=64 tokens) on p3/rtx-class instances in our lab benchmarks.
- Host CPU sys/user utilization during 10k QPS soak reduced by >=18% on targeted machine profiles.
- No regression (>2%) in median throughput for long-sequence (>1024 tokens) workloads.
tasks: Design shim API and data structures (in C++ runtime)
Implement rendezvous coalescer and quanta scheduler
NUMA hinting and memory-type detection integration
Expose shim metrics to kernel-selector and console
Add unit/integration tests with microbench harness
Run perf bench suite across instance types and collect SLO metrics
Code review and rollout in canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% rollout
acceptance_criteria: E2E perf: 95p prefill->decode latency -30% on short requests (lab)
No >2% throughput regression for long sequences
Feature toggles for coalescing and quanta size available in config
Kernel-selector successfully reads shim metrics and adjusts kernel choice
risks: Coalescing might add latency for some low-concurrency requests if window sizing is poor
NUMA misprediction could cause cross-socket memcopy regressions
Interaction with pinned-buffer registration semantics across OSes (Linux vs macOS)
Increased code complexity in host pipeline impacting maintainability
notes: Implementation will target Linux first; we will prototype using io_uring for batched submits where available, and fallback to epoll/eventfd path. We should benchmark pinned vs pageable paths and add heuristics to promote frequently-accessed buffers to pinned to increase coalesceability. Will coordinate with runtime/allocator team to expose a lightweight buffer descriptor indicating allocation domain and pin status.
comments: 2026-02-14 - Maya Chen: Spike completed. Prototype fused memcpy logic reduces syscall count by ~60% in microbench. Observed occasional 150us added tail for single-request case when window was 1ms. Need smaller adaptive window.
2026-02-21 - Arjun Patel: Implemented thread quanta release and simple per-thread backoff. Integration tests added for single-GPU and multi-GPU. Initial canary run shows promising CPU reduction.
2026-02-28 - Priya Rao (performance lead): Reviewed NUMA hints. Suggested we tie coalesce decision to recent per-socket memory throughput stats; added to backlog to capture dynamic node behavior.
2026-03-05 - Security: Reviewed memory handling for pinned buffers. No immediate issues but flagged that pinned promotion may need audit logs when enabled on Private deployments.
2026-03-09 - Arjun Patel: Canary at 10% saw 32% 95p improvement for small requests on rtx-a5000 lab cluster. Filed follow-up ENG-246804 to tune kernel-selector thresholds based on shim metrics.
